answer.evidence: The entire lantern post is drawn in pure front elevation with perfectly horizontal bands and bars. The collar under the lantern (rows 12-14) and the base (rows 25-30) are drawn dead-on as flat horizontal rectangles with no visible top surface foreshortened toward the viewer.

answer.main_body: lamp post with lantern and base
answer.evidence: The entire lamp post is drawn as a flat 2D front elevation (side-scroller view). The lantern shelf (rows 12-14), lantern glass, roof eaves (rows 5-7), and the stepped base (rows 25-30) are all rendered with straight horizontal bands with zero foreshortened top surfaces visible.

The entire street lamp is drawn in pure front elevation with straight horizontal bands. The stepped plinth at the base (rows 25-31), the collar under the lantern (rows 12-14), and the lantern frame (rows 8-11) show no foreshortened top surfaces at all, and the cap is rendered flatly from the front.

The lantern and post are drawn in pure front elevation with straight horizontal bands for the eaves (rows 6-7) and lantern bracket (rows 12-14). No top surface or downward perspective is visible on the main lantern structure, and base plinths do not qualify.
